fields.label: Level
fields.help: As labelled on the request. A distance alone ("2", "2cm") prints as "2 cm from AV". Recommended levels: at least 2 cm above the dentate line (ERNICA 2020), or 2, 3 and 4 cm from the anal verge (Ambartsumyan 2020).

fields.label: Submucosa
fields.help: Sufficient: at least 3 mm across with a third or more submucosa (IWG 2009; ERNICA 2020), or submucosa as thick as the mucosa (AJCP 2023). With scant or no submucosa, ganglion cells cannot be judged absent.

reference.title: Biopsy adequacy
reference.intro: Each biopsy is judged on its own: enough submucosa, and colorectal rather than anal canal mucosa (IWG 2009; APSA HDIG 2019).

groups.heading: Sufficient submucosa
points: At least 3 mm across, with a third or more submucosa (IWG 2009; ERNICA 2020)
Ambartsumyan 2020: 2-3 mm with 50% or more submucosa
AJCP 2023: submucosa as thick as the mucosa; under a third risks sampling error

groups.heading: Too distal
points: Squamous or transitional mucosa places the biopsy in the anal canal
Ganglion cells there still exclude Hirschsprung disease; their absence does not diagnose it (IWG 2009)
The submucosal hypoganglionic zone reaches 10-25 mm above the dentate line, with age (IWG 2009)

reference.note: Room for your own photographs: no openly licensed images of an adequate or a too-distal suction biopsy were found.

fields.label: Anal canal mucosa
fields.help: Squamous or transitional mucosa marks a biopsy from the anal canal. Ganglion cells found there still exclude Hirschsprung disease; their absence does not diagnose it (IWG 2009; Ambartsumyan 2020).

fields.label: H&E sections examined
fields.help: The IWG 2009 asks for the number of sections evaluated; it suggests 50-75 H&E sections at first. No minimum has been validated.

fields.label: Submucosal ganglion cells
fields.help: A single unequivocal submucosal ganglion cell excludes Hirschsprung disease when the submucosa is adequate (IWG 2009). Mimics: endothelial cells, plasma cells, histiocytes, glia and CMV-infected cells (AJCP 2023).

reference.title: Ganglion cells
reference.intro: Look next to the muscularis mucosae and next to the muscularis propria, where the yield is highest (AJCP 2023).

groups.heading: Ganglion cells
points: Abundant amphophilic cytoplasm, eccentric round nucleus, conspicuous nucleolus (Ambartsumyan 2020)
Usually grouped, in contact with neuropil
Immature, in neonates: less cytoplasm, stippled chromatin, inconspicuous nucleolus

images.caption: Submucosal ganglion cells (arrows) in a rectal biopsy without Hirschsprung disease (H&E).
images.credit: Beltman et al., Virchows Arch 2022, Fig 1a (cropped)

groups.heading: Mimics
points: Endothelial cells: red cells in tiny lumina are a clue
Plasma cells, especially on frozen sections
Histiocytes, glia and CMV-infected cells
One candidate cell in many sections: share the case (AJCP 2023)

fields.label: Myenteric ganglion cells
fields.help: Many biopsies sent as full-thickness hold only mucosa and submucosa (AJCP 2023): choose Not sampled when the muscularis propria is missing.

fields.label: Submucosal nerves
fields.help: Hypertrophic: at least two nerves of 40 µm or more in one high-power field (AJCP 2023; Monforte-Muñoz 1998). Less reliable after 6-12 months of age; may be absent in total colonic aganglionosis, long-segment disease and premature infants.

groups.heading: Hypertrophic
points: At least two nerves of 40 µm or more in one high-power field (AJCP 2023)
Normal infant submucosal nerves measure 10-30 µm (Monforte 2025)
Ganglion cells with hypertrophic nerves: consider the transition zone of very-short-segment disease (Ambartsumyan 2020)

images.caption: Hypertrophic submucosal nerve fibres (arrows) and no ganglion cells: Hirschsprung disease (H&E).
images.credit: Beltman et al., Virchows Arch 2022, Fig 1b (cropped)

groups.heading: May be absent
points: Total colonic aganglionosis
Long-segment disease, neonates and premature infants (IWG 2009; AJCP 2023)
After 6-12 months, nerves over 40 µm can be normal (AJCP 2023; Kapur 2016)

fields.label: Calretinin
fields.help: Count only fibrils in the lamina propria and muscularis mucosae, and ganglion cells: extrinsic submucosal nerves can stain in aganglionic bowel (AJCP 2023; Ambartsumyan 2020). Mast cells are a limited internal control.

groups.heading: Normal pattern
points: Granular fibrils in the lamina propria, muscularis mucosae and superficial submucosa (Kapur 2009)
Ganglion cells stain, cell bodies and processes

images.caption: Calretinin-positive nerve fibres in the lamina propria: normal pattern.
images.credit: Hiradfar et al., Iran J Basic Med Sci 2012, Fig 1A (cropped)

images.caption: Calretinin in a rectal biopsy without Hirschsprung disease: positive fibres at the base of the mucosa and in the submucosa.
images.credit: Beltman et al., Virchows Arch 2022, Fig 1e (cropped)

groups.heading: Aganglionic pattern
points: No fibrils in the lamina propria or muscularis mucosae
Mast cells still stain: round or oval, fine uniform staining
Fibrils persist in the proximal 1-2 cm of aganglionic bowel, so their presence does not exclude very-short-segment disease (Kapur 2014)
Freeze-thaw can remove calretinin: not after AChE on the same tissue

images.caption: Calretinin in Hirschsprung disease: no immunoreactive fibres.
images.credit: Beltman et al., Virchows Arch 2022, Fig 1f (cropped)

fields.label: Acetylcholinesterase
fields.help: Frozen tissue only (10-15 µm sections; IWG 2009). Hirschsprung pattern: abundant coarse fibres in the muscularis mucosae and lamina propria. False negatives in neonates, total colonic aganglionosis and ultrashort disease.

groups.heading: Normal pattern
points: Sparse, thin fibres, mostly in the submucosa and muscularis mucosae (IWG 2009)

images.caption: Acetylcholinesterase without Hirschsprung disease: focal fibres confined to the submucosa and muscularis mucosae (frozen section).
images.credit: Beltman et al., Virchows Arch 2022, Fig 1c (cropped)

groups.heading: Hirschsprung pattern
points: Abundant coarse fibres in the muscularis mucosae and lamina propria (IWG 2009)
False negatives in the first weeks of life, in total colonic aganglionosis and in ultrashort disease

images.caption: Acetylcholinesterase in Hirschsprung disease: aberrant positive fibres (brown) in the lamina propria.

fields.label: Diagnosis line
fields.help: Auto: ganglion cells present; none identified, with the Hirschsprung statement when hypertrophic nerves, absent calretinin fibrils or increased acetylcholinesterase fibres are recorded (IWG 2009: findings "consistent with" Hirschsprung disease); or inadequate for evaluation when there is too little submucosa or the biopsy includes anal canal mucosa (IWG 2009 Box 1).

example.caseTitle: Rectal suction biopsies at two levels
